Announced the coalition would not oppose the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013 given the state of the budget, but criticised its sixth cut to the low-income super co-contribution, halving the maximum from $1,000 to $500 and bringing total cuts to more than $3.3 billion, and noted a $1 billion surplus forecast six months ago has become a $19 billion deficit.

Argued for the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013, noting almost 32 million superannuation accounts existed as of June 2012, nearly three per worker, and welcomed listing the National Boer War Memorial Association as a deductible gift recipient to help fund a national memorial on Anzac Parade, noting 23,000 Australians served and 589 died in the Boer War, with the project already backed by a $200,000 Department of Veterans' Affairs seeding grant.

Argued that the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013 contains eight schedules covering film tax offsets, disaster recovery payments, GST instalments, deductible gift recipients, superannuation accounts, co-contributions, dependency offsets and taxation of financial arrangements, highlighting documentary definitions and support for small businesses.

Supported adding six entities to the deductible gift recipient list, particularly the ANZAC Centenary Public Fund, saying tax deductibility would help communities contribute to commemorations of Australia's involvement in World War I-1914 to 1918 and recognise service personnel.

Argued that the bill restores the previously understood meaning of documentary for film tax offsets, exempts specified disaster payments from income tax, supports GST instalment users, adds six deductible gift recipients, consolidates multiple superannuation accounts, changes co-contribution thresholds, consolidates eight dependency offsets and clarifies taxation of financial arrangements.

The coalition requested separate votes on two tax bills, the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 1) Bill 2013 and the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013, and both were ultimately passed.
